findings.description: The Requirement body states: 'index.ts:1028-1041 awaits initialize() on all four of these stores during bootstrap' and the Trace Links table cites the same range server/src/index.ts:1028-1041 with the note 'bootstrap awaits initialize() on all four of these stores, each of which flushes unguarded'. Reading the actual file (sed -n '1028,1042p' server/src/index.ts) shows only three awaited initialize() calls inside 1028-1041: commandPresetService.initialize() (1029), terminalShortcutService.initialize() (1032), recoveryOptionService.initialize() (1035). The fourth store's call, workspaceService.initialize(), is at line 1042 -- one line outside the cited range (workspaceService itself is constructed at 1041, initialize() awaited at 1042). The cited line range does not contain what the text and trace-link note both claim it contains.
findings.suggested_action: Widen the trace link and body citation to server/src/index.ts:1028-1042 (or 1028-1043) so it actually spans all four initialize() calls, or cite workspaceService's initialize() separately.

findings.description: GitHub issue #24 explicitly names a second contributing structural cause beyond the fixed temp-path collision: 'dev 서버 기동 스크립트(dev.js) 및 관련 파일 감시(watch) 로직 확인 필요' -- i.e. every tsx watcher/dev instance restarting on every shared source-file change, which is what causes many processes to hit flushToDisk() at once in the first place. The requirement text, statement, rationale and ACs never mention dev.js, the watcher/restart structure, or file-watch scoping anywhere (verified by grepping the full block text for 'dev.js', 'watcher', 'watch' -- the only match is the incidental 'npx tsx --test' token in Verification Method, unrelated to the watcher). REL-BGSTAB-022 fixes the write-race consequence but is silent on whether the watcher-restart-storm cause is in or out of scope; it is neither addressed nor explicitly declared out of scope anywhere in the block or in the SRS document's Scope Boundaries section.
findings.suggested_action: Add an explicit sentence (in the Requirement narrative or as a new Out-of-Scope-style note) stating that the multi-watcher restart-storm structure in dev.js is a separate/deferred concern, or open a companion requirement/issue reference for it.

findings.description: The document's '### In Scope' list (lines 15-24) enumerates: runtime-configured caps for WebSocket/terminal/snapshot/terminal-runtime, browser WebSocket backpressure, visible terminal output scheduling, snapshot localStorage budget/tombstone TTL, hidden terminal runtime LRU residency, split WebSocket handshake/routing/fallback, negotiated binary wire format, and non-2002 validation requirements. None of these bullets cover JSON store publication/persistence-file concurrency at all -- the entire subject matter of REL-BGSTAB-022 (CommandPresetService/WorkspaceService/TerminalShortcutService/RecoveryOptionService flush-to-disk races). '### Out of Scope' (lines 26-31) likewise says nothing about store persistence. REL-BGSTAB-020/021, which are the closest siblings and also deal with flushToDisk, are already in this same document without their subject matter appearing in the Scope Boundaries list either, so this may be a pre-existing gap in the document rather than one newly introduced by 022 -- but 022 does not correct it, and adding a new requirement in an uncovered domain without updating Scope Boundaries leaves the document's own In/Out-of-Scope lists unable to justify the requirement's presence.
findings.suggested_action: Add a Scope Boundaries bullet covering server-side JSON store persistence/publication (or note that REL-BGSTAB-020/021/022 sit under an implicit 'persistence' scope that should be named explicitly).

findings.evidence_path: docs/spec/30.buildergate-stability.srs.md:6003-6028 (#### Requirement narrative, 'Second, the process dies rather than logging' paragraph)
findings.description: The #### Requirement section enumerates 'Three distinct failures' as the problem being solved, and the second is framed at length ('the process dies rather than logging ... The race window is therefore opened by every start ... the consequence is a dead instance rather than a warning'). No AC (AC-1..AC-8) tests any change to index.ts's fatal bootstrap behavior (unguarded initialize() + process.exit(1) in the catch at index.ts:1654-1657). The Trace Links table does mark those two index.ts locations with relation 'verifies' rather than 'addition_site', which is some evidence they are cited only as motivating context and not as sites this requirement changes -- but nothing in the Requirement statement or ACs explicitly disclaims fixing failure #2, so a reader following the 'three failures this requirement addresses' framing could reasonably expect an AC asserting the server no longer exits fatally on an exhausted-retry or non-transient rejection during bootstrap, and none exists (AC-4/AC-5 only assert what the publish call itself does, not what index.ts does with that rejection).
findings.suggested_action: Either add an AC (or an explicit disclaimer in the Requirement text) stating that changing index.ts's fatal-on-reject bootstrap behavior is out of scope for this requirement, since AC-4/AC-5 still allow initialize() to reject and index.ts's catch is unchanged.
